findings: Only generated report cleanup and its controls/receipt fields changed. Exact validate_rejection, the existing eight synthetic reader controls and report glob function bodies (excluding between-function blank separators) and original Bazel argv remain byte-identical to the reviewed de4 source.

A report must be a regular file with no leaf reparse attribute before read/chmod/unlink. Only an actual Windows READONLY bit causes chmod; other I/O errors propagate. The removed original report bytes/hash and observed attribute are recorded; no source path is selected for removal.

Exactly one prior report for each log/XML suffix is required. Successful removal is checked before the actual no-Job mutation; fresh report uniqueness and the original 0/2/31 survivor failure/XML/exit-3 requirements remain.

The two new cleanup controls create only owned temporary files, require a true Windows READONLY observation, remove that file, and reject a real directory without removing it. They are separated from native product acceptance.
limitations: Static byte/diff review only; no Windows file operation, Python control, Bazel mutant or native test was run by this reviewer. The earlier WinError5 remains an actual failed qualification and is not reclassified.

This validates the bounded known generated-report path selection in the reviewed workflow design, not arbitrary hostile concurrent filesystem replacement. The helper reads each report completely and does not claim a separate report memory/RSS cap.
The original subprocess/job timeout and ordinary finally-restoration boundaries from prior review remain. This is not a production or original-test acceptance claim.
